To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the apoptosis of beta cells in spontaneous diabetes in the non-obese diabetic mouse model occurs at low levels and is not localised to beta cells, while apoptosis of beta cells after cyclophoshamide-acceleration of beta-cell destruction occurs more frequently and is localised to CD8+ cells.

the frequency of apoptosis within islets correlated with progression of beta-cell loss with age, and that the rarity of detectable apoptosis of beta cells in spontaneous, pre-diabetic NOD mice reflects the rapid clearance and/or rapid destruction of these cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the destruction of beta cells, the insulin-producing cells, in the pancreas of non-obese diabetic mice.
the mechanisms of beta-cell death in spontaneous and cyclo-phosphamide-accel-erated diabetes in the NOD mouse.
the mechanisms of beta-cell destruction in the spontaneous autoimmune disease, type 1 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
apoptosis of the beta cells is the cause of the diabetes in NOD-mice, but that it is not the only cause of the diabetes.

the frequency of apoptosis is low and is not beta-cell specific in spontaneous pre-diabetes in NOD mice, and the frequency of apoptosis peaks in the beta-cell depleted islets in cyclophosphamid-accelerated NOD diabetes.
the frequency of apoptosis correlates with the progression of the beta cell destruction with age.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of apoptosis correlated with the progression and acceleration of beta-cell loss with age.
the beta cells are dying slowly in spontaneous diabetes, but dying quickly after cyclophoshamide treatment.
apoptosis is a major cause of beta-cell death in NOD mice with cyclophospamide-accelerant diabetes but a minor cause of beta-cell loss in the spontaneous form of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
apoptosis of beta cells is not a major cause of diabetes in NOD.
the destruction of beta cells is a gradual process.
beta-cell death in spontaneous diabetes occurs gradually and is most likely due to a gradual decline in beta-cell mass.
